answer: Every identity climbs the same ladder from the bottom: each rung is a task drawn only after the previous rung is attested, and its reward sits in escrow until the identity has stood on three consecutive rungs. A new head starts at zero and cannot buy, borrow, or skip a rung, so the nth clone costs the same full sequence of real work as the first, paid in parallel rather than once. The onyx ledger records which rung each key reached, a pearl is granted per rung, and the vault releases nothing to an identity younger than the ladder. A thousand heads mean a thousand ladders climbed at once.
